en: O best of beings, please tell me that which is to be recited at the commencement of all undertakings, during bad dreams, and when inauspicious sights are seen. || 1 ||
By this, undertakings are accomplished, evil dreams are pacified, and the removal of all observed inauspicious sights occurs. || 2 ||
O great sage, the man who constantly remembers Janārdana— the Lord of beings and the Teacher of the world—
destroys all evils without exception and accomplishes every task that he desires.
Listen further as I speak; O best of the twice-born, I shall tell you everything that is auspicious, which always bestows the accomplishment of all goals and destroys every single sin. (4)

May Hari, in whom the world of moving and non-moving beings is established, who is the cause of the world within the three realms, and who protects and devours the world, always be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May Hari, the Supreme Lord— who is expansive through the natures of ether, water, air, fire, and earth, yet subtler than the subtle due to his atomic nature, and who is neither gross nor minute— be for the constant increase of my auspiciousness.
Since there is nothing whatsoever superior to that infinite Person who is without beginning or middle,
may Hari— the cause of causes, the Lord of the Supreme Lord— be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Lord Hari, who assumes the forms of Hiraṇyagarbha, Acyuta, and Rudra, and who creates, protects, and destroys the entire universe as the foremost of the Guṇas, always bring about the increase of my auspiciousness.
May Hari— who is beyond the gods, supreme among the asuras, beyond the ascetics, and the highest of sages,
and who transcends all else— ever grant the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari—the Lord of the Supreme Lords, who bestows liberation upon those sages who are free from stain when meditated upon, and who is delightful to the mind—always be present for the increase of my auspiciousness. (10)

May that Hari— the Supreme Lord of lords, who is pure and utterly pure, and who protects the world by assuming the forms of Surendra, Vaivasvata, Vittapa, Ambupa, and Svarūpa— be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari—who is indeed liberated from the accumulation of sins gathered over many births simply by the chanting of His name, and who is the fire for the fuel of sin—be forever pure for the increase of my auspiciousness. 12.

May that Hari, by whom this earth was lifted from the netherworld (rasātala) and who is the cause of the creation and sustenance of the entire universe, be the root of my being for the increase of auspiciousness. 13.

May that Hari, the Lord of lords, whose feet are the Vedas, whose belly is the moving and unmoving world, whose body-hair is all the sages without exception, and whose mouth is the sacrifices— may he always be the master for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Lord Hari, who assumed the form of a boar, whose body consists of all the limbs of sacrifice, and whose very person is praised by the lords of lords, always grant the increase of my auspiciousness. 15.

May Hari— the Lord of Sacrifice, the Person of Sacrifice— who, having churned the waters produced from all the oceans, sustained the earth and the world— always be for the increase of my auspiciousness.
May that Acyuta Hari, who supports the earth while his feet rest upon the multitude of serpents at the base of Pātāla, and for whom no comparison exists—may he increase my auspiciousness. (17)
May that Hari, whose thundering roar is repeatedly heard by Sanandana and others dwelling in Janaloka as they cry out "Victory!", always exist for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari, whose body was bent down by the best of yogins as he rose with great speed toward the sky, seizing the earth from the single vast ocean—may he always bring about the increase of my auspiciousness. (19)
May that Lord Hari—the ancient Supreme Person who in former times slew the great asura Hiraṇyākṣa while in the form of a boar—be my husband for the increase of my auspiciousness. 20.
May that Lord Hari, who assumed a divine form as Nṛsiṃha with terrifying fangs to destroy the fear of the gods and protect the world, always be present for the increase of my auspiciousness. (21)
May that Acyuta, who severed the fears of the world with his hand-lotuses— terrible as saws for rending the chest of the lord of the Daityas— grant us protection.
May Hari be for the increase of my auspiciousness. || 22 ||
May that Hari— who made all the faces of the quarters pure with the brilliance shining from between his tusks,
and who terrified the Dānavas with his roar— be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari, the Man-Lion, who removes the suffering of all the worlds, grant the increase of my auspiciousness—he by the mere chanting of whose name a person attains liberation from great fear, without a doubt. (24)

May that divine lion, Hari, whose eyes are like flickering flames, exist for the increase of my auspiciousness—he upon whom the clouds burst apart on all sides when struck by the wind from the whirling of his mane. 25.
When the orb of rays had dissolved into the light of his eyes, the splendor of the sun did not shine even slightly;
how much less so that of the moon? May that Hari, who assumes such a divine form, grant the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Great Hari, the remover of the suffering of all worlds, whose most wonderful deeds are eternally praised by the lords of all gods and lords of men, be for the increase of my auspiciousness. (27)

The Daityas flee, the deities bow down, the Rākṣasas perish, and enemies retreat at the mere chanting of his name; may that Hari, whose mane is of wondrous form, grant the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari, who as Vāmana purified the world with the Ṛgveda, adorned it with the Yajurveda, and destroyed all sins with the resonance of the Sāmaveda, always bring about the increase of my auspiciousness. (29)

May that Hari, Vāmana, whose divine form and beauty was beheld, by whom the earth attained sanctity through the placement of his feet and the sky through the chanting of the Ṛg and Yajur Vedas, be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Vāmana, who is identical with the entire universe—that Hari, at whose departure from the sacrifice the earth together with its oceans bowed down in exhaustion—always be for the increase of my auspiciousness. (31)

May that Hari, the Dwarf (Vāmana), who dwells within the seven worlds and who, upon entering the most wonderful great sacrifice of the Lord of Daityas, caused it to be agitated by the great Asuras, grant the increase of my auspiciousness.

May Hari— who was praised in due order by the hosts of gods dwelling in heaven, by humans situated on the earth, and by sky-dwellers in the atmosphere, and who always moves forth— be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari— the God of gods, the Lord of the lords of the worlds— who, having traversed the earth, the sky, and heaven, bestowed the celestial realm upon the Lord of the Maruts, grant the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari, who bestowed the supreme grace upon Balarāma— making him equal to the status of Indra in an instant— and who always grants a share of the sacrifices to the gods, be for the increase of my auspiciousness.

May that Hari— the enemy of Kaiṭabha, the slayer of Madhu, who reclines upon the waters— be for the increase of my auspiciousness, he by whom in ancient times all the Vedas were recovered from the netherworld (rasātala) while assuming the form of a water-creeper.

May that Hari, the best of the Bhṛgus, who rendered the earth devoid of Kṣatriyas and repeatedly lopped off the forest of his arms, be for the increase of my auspiciousness—He who [slain] Kārtavīrya. 37.
He who, having slain Vālin of fierce prowess and having bound the Ten-faced one with a bridge over the ocean,
also slew the other night-stalkers.
May Hari be for the increase of my auspiciousness. || 38 ||
May that Hari—who as a child overturned a cart, who broke Yama-Arjuna, who slew his enemy Kaṃsa, and who crushed Cāṇūra and the others—always be for the increase of my auspiciousness. (39)
May the Lord Hari, who at dawn bears the Sudarśana discus— pure as the rays of the thousand-rayed sun—
and also the Kaumodakī mace, as Ananta, be for the increase of my auspiciousness.
May Hari, the Lord of Lords, who bears the conch shell— pure as the luster of snow, the moon, jasmine, and crystal, and filled with the breath from his mouth—
even while carrying it at midday, grant the increase of my auspiciousness.

Likewise, in the afternoon, may Hari— the one who bears the beauty of a blossoming lotus upon his chest and whose eyes are like the broad petals of a wide-spreading lotus— be for the increase of my auspiciousness.
May Hari, the Lord of lords, the beginningless Blessed One, who exists in all times, in all places, and in all activities through all his own forms, be for the increase of my auspiciousness. (43)
O Dālbhya, a person devoted to Viṣṇu who recites this is liberated from all sins;
likewise, all his undertakings attain success.
He obtains those objects exactly as he desires. || 44 ||
When this hymn is recited by one who is ever-vigilant in the practice of listening, bad dreams come to rest;
O Lord, the undertaking of such a person swiftly reaches fulfillment.
And the God of gods destroys his sins. || 45 ||

What in this world, and even in the next, bestows upon men that which is auspicious, the supreme state, the constant accomplishment of goals, and prosperity that is free from obstacles and yields abundant fruit?
O Dālbhya, that which cannot be accomplished even by those whose minds are devoted to Viṣṇu.
Devendra attained lordship over the three worlds, Kārtavīrya achieved perfection throughout the three worlds,
and Vaideha reached the supreme state by propitiating Viṣṇu.
For Viṣṇu, once attained, indeed bestows all fruits.
O Dālbhya, in all undertakings, during bad dreams,
and likewise upon seeing anything inauspicious, a wise man should recite [the name of] Viṣṇu with a one-pointed mind.
Evil influences and terrible afflictions from the planets are pacified;
undertakings succeed, and one attains supreme merit. (49)
Hari, praised with auspicious hymns of praise, bestows blessings;
bearing unimpaired power, he provides protection through all his forms.
The Auspicious Hymn contained within the Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara is complete.
